answer: Enroll each earning key as sole holder of one meteor-scatter call sign, mast surveyed in a named canyon so the far end sits past the radio horizon. Before cutoff that mast returns a seed-tagged frame reflected from ionization in a listed comet debris stream; a public listener records the Doppler and call sign. One radio completes a single hop in time, so every added key funds its own license, mast, and site. Working figures only: $3,200 a station and $70 monthly rent; eighty extras run about $256,000 plus $5,600 that month.
